title: Fact-Checker Roadmap
summary: Build a career verifying public claims, images, videos and news reports through evidence-based research, source verification, digital investigation and clear explanations that help audiences distinguish reliable information from misleading content.

facts.Current degree: BJMC / B.A. Journalism & Mass Communication – Data Journalism / Fact-Checking
facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a three-year bachelor's degree, with an optional fourth-year honours route if offered by your university. The long-term planning horizon extends from 2026 to 2046.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: A portfolio of documented fact-checks, source trails, image and video verification exercises, and entry-level newsroom experience.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Expertise in political claims, public health, misinformation, visual verification, regional-language content or investigative research.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Senior fact-checking, verification desk leadership, investigations editing or research management.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Leadership in information integrity, advanced verification workflows and responsible use of AI-assisted research.

blocks.text: The aim is to learn a repeatable verification process: identify the exact claim, trace its original source, find independent evidence, assess context and publish a transparent conclusion.

rows.text: A fact-check of a straightforward public claim.
One report showing the claim, source links, evidence and conclusion.
A verification log with image matches, dates and original-source checks.
A video verification exercise using keyframes and contextual searches.
A documented report showing the relevant frames, search trail and limitations.
A fact-check based on an official dataset or public document.
A source-linked article with calculations and an explanation of what the data can establish.
A series of fact-checks on a chosen topic or in a regional language.
Three to five fact-checks with primary sources and transparent methodology.
A newsroom-style project or fact-checking internship.
One editor-reviewed fact-check and a documented research workflow.
An investigation into a recurring misinformation pattern.
A case study with source mapping, evidence records and ethical safeguards.
A reproducible verification project or research capstone.
A final report, source archive where lawful, methodology and limitations statement.

blocks.text: Four-year honours variant

If your university offers a four-year honours programme, use Year 4 for a research-intensive misinformation study, advanced verification project or dissertation on information integrity. Confirm the current degree structure and eligibility with your university.

blocks.label: Evolve and stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Progress from checking individual claims to identifying misinformation patterns, training verification teams and designing newsroom standards. Use AI tools as research aids rather than final authorities. Maintain evidence trails, protect sources, correct errors transparently and distinguish falsehoods from claims that are merely unproven or missing context.

blocks.label: Eligibility note
blocks.text: Check each notice for education, age, location, language and experience requirements. The Prime Minister's Internship Scheme has distinct eligibility conditions, including a restriction related to full-time education, so it should not be assumed to be available to a full-time undergraduate student.
Fact-checking is a practical profession. A certificate can help structure learning, but transparent research and accurate published work are stronger evidence of ability.

blocks.text: Student Researcher / Fact-Checking Intern

blocks.label: Year 3–5

blocks.text: Fact-Checker / Senior Verification Researcher

blocks.label: Year 9–14
blocks.text: Verification Editor / Investigations Editor

blocks.label: Year 14+
blocks.text: Head of Verification / Research Director / Independent Journalist
These milestones are illustrative. Progress depends on editorial experience, accuracy, specialist knowledge and opportunities; independent researchers may follow a different route.
PhD routes
A PhD is optional for newsroom fact-checking but may suit someone interested in academic research, teaching or developing verification methods.

blocks.text: Fact-checking practices, newsroom standards and investigative reporting.

blocks.text: Digital archives, information retrieval and the reliability of online information.
Check each university's eligibility, entrance requirements, supervisor availability and funding rules before applying.

2040–2046: remain relevant. Build expertise in advanced verification, source protection, digital forensics, statistical reasoning and editorial leadership. AI-generated images, synthetic audio and automated content will make transparent methods and independent corroboration increasingly important. Your long-term value will come from showing how you reached a conclusion, communicating uncertainty honestly and correcting errors openly.
